newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX closes at fourth record high in row.
newsitem.headline: German DAX closes at fourth record high in row.

text.p: Germany's DAX index of leading shares stormed higher on Tuesday and ended bourse dealings at its fourth record close in a row, after the dollar soared to a 23-month high against the mark.
Strength in German government bonds, also at record highs, provided additional support for the market.
The DAX 30-share index closed floor trade at 2,886.98 points, marking a gain of 28.38 points, or 0.99 percent.
"Everybody who was in the market is happy and everybody else is being forced to pile in," said one trader. "Psychologically the DAX is already at 2,900 points."
But the index could not mount the psychological and technical level of 2,900 points on Tuesday, faltering at a bourse record of 2,895.19 points, and an IBIS record of 2,897.24 points.

The U.S. currency rose above the crucial 1.56 mark level overnight following comments by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing and New York Federal Reserve Bank William McDonough on the dollar becoming more important in the run up to European monetary union.
Dollar strength benefited the German export-oriented chemicals companies in particular.
Shares in BASF AG jumped 3.4 percent, to end bourse dealings up 1.99 marks at 60 marks, while Bayer AG rose three percent, or 1.93 marks to 64.55 marks.
"The climb in chemicals has been extreme," said one trader.
Shares in automakers, major exporters, also forged ahead, Daimler-Benz AG gaining 2.90 marks to 105 marks and BMW AG up 36.50 marks, or 3.6 percent at 1,047.50 marks.
Meanwhile shares in Europe's largest carmaker Volkswagen ended up 5.50 marks at 592.50 marks, as bargain hunters moved in to buy shares at lower prices.

In early electronic IBIS dealings the stock had dropped over three percent to touch 574 marks, after a U.S. judge denied the firm's motion to dismiss General Motors Corp.'s remaining industrial espionage claims against the German carmaker.
